# Preface {.unnumbered}

This book is a worked, end-to-end analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing with paired T-cell receptor (TCR) sequencing, built from the workflow I use for CD4⁺ T-cell projects. Every chapter is fully reproducible from public data. Code is folded under each figure: click **Code** to expand it.

## Dataset

The analysis uses the public dataset [GEO GSE344965](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE344965), lung CD4⁺ T cells from mice treated with a TNFR2 agonist or a control VHH. In the original study, eight- to ten-week-old female C57BL/6 mice received 3 mg/kg TNFR2 agonist (i.v.), 1 mg/kg IL-2 mutein (s.c.) or 3 mg/kg control VHH (i.v.), and lungs were collected five days later. CD4⁺ T cells from 12 mice were hashtag-multiplexed and profiled on a single 10x Genomics GEM-X 5′ library with gene expression, hashtag (HTO) and V(D)J-T libraries.

This book compares the **TNFR2 agonist** arm with the **control** arm (four mice each). The IL-2 mutein arm is excluded to keep a clean two-group, replicate-aware design.

| Condition | Treatment | Mice (GEO label) | Samples in this book |
|---|---|---|---|
| Control | Control VHH, 3 mg/kg i.v. | M01–M04 | Ctrl_1 – Ctrl_4 |
| TNFR2a | TNFR2 agonist, 3 mg/kg i.v. | M05–M08 | TNFR2a_1 – TNFR2a_4 |

: Study design used in this book {#tbl-design}

GEO provides the authors' processed Seurat object rather than raw Cell Ranger outputs, so the workflow starts from their raw RNA and HTO counts and per-cell TCR CDR3 sequences. All downstream steps (QC, normalisation, integration, clustering, annotation, clonotype reconstruction, differential expression, pathway and trajectory analysis) are re-run here from those counts.

## Questions

1. Which CD4⁺ T-cell states are present in the lung, and how does TNFR2 agonism shift their composition?
2. Does TNFR2 agonism drive clonal expansion, and in which states do expanded clones reside?
3. Which transcriptional programs change with treatment, assessed with replicate-aware pseudobulk models?
4. How do clonal expansion and treatment interact at the level of gene expression and pathways?

## Workflow

| Chapter | Main methods |
|---|---|
| Preprocessing | Data import, HTO demultiplexing (HTODemux), TCR contig reconstruction |
| QC and integration | DoubletFinder, QC filtering, SCTransform v2, Harmony |
| Dimensionality reduction | Leiden resolution sweep, clustree, marker detection |
| Clustering and annotation | Canonical marker review, composition per mouse |
| Refined clustering | Curated state labels |
| TCR clonotype analysis | Chain-aware clonotypes, expansion, sharing, CDR3 motifs |
| Differential expression | Pseudobulk edgeR quasi-likelihood per state |
| Clonotype-informed DE | Expanded vs singleton, treatment within expanded clones |
| Pathway analysis | ORA and GSEA (KEGG, Reactome, GO BP) |
| Trajectory | Slingshot and tradeSeq |

## Reproducing the analysis

```bash
git clone https://github.com/SerenaGall/tcr-scrnaseq-showcase
cd tcr-scrnaseq-showcase
quarto render
```

The first chapter downloads the GEO object (~530 MB) into `data/raw/`. Rendered outputs are stored in `_freeze/`, so the website can be rebuilt without re-running the analysis.
